title: How Common Are Intentional GAAP Violations? Estimates from a Dynamic Model

scopes.description: Complete documented raw preparation and build of normalized revenue-recognition-error data, then SMM estimation, implied-manipulation inference and R table compilation. The paper package’s raw preparation is explicitly illustrative and its full source-data construction is not closed.

Use the supplied author-prepared normalized dataparam MAT and value weights to rerun the revenue-recognition SMM, create the gmmobjres solution, invert model-implied manipulation to CSV, then compile the supported parameter table and pooled Table 8 subset. The packaged SMM-result MAT and manipulation CSV also let the R table branch consume reference outputs directly. Supported outputs are Table 4 parameter estimates and pooled 2003–2010 incidence/value-weighted stock-price bias; withheld identities, years and adjustment factors prevent broader Table 8 outputs.

issues.description: In momentsSim.m, line 57 assigns zeros to `nmnaip_temp` using an `isnan(nmanip_temp)` mask, leaving the intended `nmanip_temp` matrix unchanged. Lines 58–61 build the manipulation history and reverse five-period cumulative filter from `nmanip_temp`; vectsim.m places NaNs outside follow-up, so those NaNs can propagate through the reverse cumulative sum and prevent the stated last-five-period restriction from trimming the history. The spelling alone does not create an undefined-variable crash in MATLAB; the supported finding is ineffective cleanup of the matrix later used.

The author explicitly says the SAS preprocessing snippets cannot run as supplied and are illustrative. The documented raw-to-final workflow also requires R import/clean/merge, manual identifier verification, Equilar/BoardEx executive matching, restatement-to-executive merging and normalization for which no complete runnable driver is supplied. This is separate from the prepared-data analysis route.

The full-preparation code does not supply producers for `equilar.equilar_gvkey_link` or `struct_manip.crsp_xpf`, and leaves setup/aliases such as `equilar`, `biglib`, `struct`, `mylib` and `mycrsp` unresolved. The BS snippet writes `mylib.t_bill`, while the intrinsic-price snippet reads `mycrsp.t_bill`; no included mapping establishes those as the same table. The commented `&idvars` note does not define the macro. Retain these setup/producer mappings as unknown rather than reconstructing them.

The illustrative get_price_function.py uses Python 2 `itertools.izip`, pandas DataFrame `.ix`, and SQLAlchemy Engine `.execute`; the Python 3.12 / pandas 3.0.6 / SQLAlchemy 2.1.3 probe shows those APIs are absent. The author labels the preparation snippets as not runnable as-is, and no supported Python version or corrected script is documented. This issue affects only the raw-preparation branch, not the supplied MATLAB analysis route.

review_notes: The frozen author variant is the revenue-recognition-errors release. The supplied final MAT and value-weight file support a distinct prepared-data analysis scope; historical source collection is not made mandatory there.

Execution order for the analysis route is estimateParams.m loading dataparam -> patternsearch/SMM saving smm_*.mat and gmmobjres_*.mat -> invertPrice.m loading gmmobjres and writing manip_*.csv -> note_on_estimates.Rmd reading the SMM result, manipulation CSV and value weights.
